frase_gancho.texto: Deep tombs, clay dogs, and the masters of copper.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You leave the Maya world behind and travel to western Mexico, a region of volcanoes, lakes, and coasts that today make up Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit, Michoacán, and Guerrero. Here the elites did not raise great pyramids for their dead: they dug deep tombs beneath the earth and filled them with clay figures that show what life was like, with dogs, warriors, couples, and banquets. Later, the Purépecha built an empire that withstood the Mexica and became masters of copper. This hall begins with the oldest vessels, more than three thousand years old, and ends with a metal that rings.
